summary: Stoddard lookout: 1915 station, 1925 steel tower, rebuilt after the 1941 Marlow-Stoddard fire; state-staffed on Class 3+ fire-danger days; trail on Andorra Forest land.

facts.design: 25-foot steel tower with 10-by-10-foot wooden cab, built 1925 per the Register

staffing.status: Staffed by state employees on Class 3 or higher fire-danger days

access.note: A trailhead kiosk, quoted by the 2025 blog, describes Andorra Forest as privately owned under a conservation easement; the tower is a working state lookout, the blog author climbed it in 2025, and sources do not say whether the cab is open to visitors

visit.drive_up: Parking lot on the northeast side of NH 123 in Stoddard
visit.trail_note: Monadnock-Sunapee Greenway (white blazes) follows the tower access road; a shorter, steeper blue-blazed trail also reaches the summit

facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

events.note: Lookout station established with a wooden tower and open platform
25-foot steel tower with a 10-by-10-foot wooden cab replaced the wooden tower
Marlow-Stoddard fire of April 1941. The Register says it destroyed the tower; the 2025 blog says it destroyed the wooden structures on top
State rebuilt the tower room almost immediately, on the same steel base (blog) or rebuilt immediately (Register)
Tower being wired for two-way radio, linked to Concord headquarters
Bid advertised for cab replacement, steel reinforcement, repairs; completion not confirmed
Register visit report (September 25, 2016): good shape, needs paint, plywood over one window

corrections.why: Wikipedia gives the mountain as 2,153 ft (656 m) with a fire tower on the summit, and the hiking blog gives the elevation as 2153 ft. The Register's 1,823 ft (556 m) site elevation does not match the summit. Proposed value is the summit height; medium confidence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the fire destroyed the tower; the 2025 blog says it destroyed the wooden structures on top and the state rebuilt the room on the same steel base. The story reports both accounts; the record is unchanged.
The Register lists 1,823 ft; Wikipedia and the blog give a 2,153-ft summit. The proposed correction above uses the summit height.

notes_for_editor: The 2016 visit reports are volunteer observations on the Register. The Keene Sentinel article has no date in the fetched text. The NH state fire-tower page and a state PDF both returned HTTP 403, so state staffing and access rules rest on news and blog sources. Staffing as_of is the 2025 blog date. The 25-ft 1925 height is used only in design, not as a current height. Register coordinates (43.09236, -72.12881) and firelookout.org (43.09405, -72.13498) differ by under 1 km; not changed. Andorra Forest access rests on blog quotes from a trailhead kiosk; the kiosk sentence about opening trails is truncated in the fetched text and is not quoted. The story does not encourage climbing. The 2025 blog author climbed the tower, which the story now says; access is still listed as restricted because the cab's status is unknown. That classification is an editorial call to confirm.
